land.text: the Ottoman Eyalet of Temeşvar (1552-1716), after the Treaty of Passarowitz

predecessors.note: The page gives the Eyalet of Temeşvar as 1552-1716 and the Banat as established on 12 July 1718 "in the wake of" Passarowitz; it gives no exact treaty date and no date for the capture of Timișoara.

land.text: the Banat, "incorporated into the Kingdom of Hungary" on 23 April 1779 and divided into the counties of Torontál, Temes and Krassó

successors.note: The southern part stayed in the Military Frontier (Banat Krajina) until 1873 (see habsburg-military-frontier); the Banat was revived as the Voivodeship of Serbia and Banat of Temeswar in 1849-1860.

correction.text: the Banat region and "parts of present-day eastern Serbia along the southern Danube"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no row. The page says the province covered "the Banat region, plus parts of present-day eastern Serbia along the southern Danube from 1718 to 1739" and gives no boundary with the Tisza, the Mureș or the Carpathians, and no area. The Danube strip (25 km, Braničevo and Bor districts) is the researcher's reading.

correction.text: the Banat region alone, after "the Treaty of Belgrade returned areas along the southern Danube bank to Ottoman control"

keyframe_review.note: 1739. The Pashalik of Belgrade dossier carries the Ottoman side.

correction.text: the civil Banat of the north, after "Civil administration was introduced in northern parts under Maria Theresa" while the south became the Banatian Military Frontier (1751)

keyframe_review.note: 1751: the page puts the southern part in the Military Frontier; South Banat (Serbia) and Caraș-Severin (Romania) stand for the frontier, as in the habsburg-military-frontier dossier. Area about 20,500 km2 on the cell grid; the page gives none.

region.text: the Banat region and the strip along the southern Danube

ledger.note: 12 July 1718: the Banat of Temeswar is established in the wake of the Treaty of Passarowitz, on the former Ottoman Eyalet of Temeşvar (1552-1716).
1739: "the Treaty of Belgrade returned areas along the southern Danube bank to Ottoman control". The page does not mention Oltenia or Orșova.
1751: Maria Theresa introduces civil administration in the north; "The southern parts were excluded and the Banatian Military Frontier was set up there."
6 June 1778: the province "abolished"; on 23 April 1779 it was incorporated into the Kingdom of Hungary and divided into the counties of Torontál, Temes and Krassó.

wars.name: Austro-Turkish War of 1737-1739
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Belgrade (1739) returned the areas along the southern Danube bank to Ottoman control.
wars.note: The page names the treaty only; the war's years are from the Pashalik of Belgrade page (1737-1739).

certainty.note: The page gives no frontier line; the Danube strip and the Carpathian side are approximate.

notes: Cliopatria has no row. One page opened (budget 1-2 pages for a state with three keyframes). Gaps: the Tisza, Mureș and Carpathian boundaries (page silent), Oltenia 1718-1739 (page silent), the date of the capture of Timișoara in 1716, and the 1848 Serbian Vojvodina. The Voivodeship of Serbia and Banat of Temeswar (1849-1860, eleven years) needs its own dossier; the page has only 1849 and 1860. Rulers: the governor list begins in 1716, before the Banat was founded. Type is colony: the Banat was ruled from Vienna, not from Hungary. Wikidata id null (unreachable).
